messages:
ben.customer: hey team — we rotated our Key Vault key (BYOK) and immediately saw a flood of envelope unwrap failures from our Redwood Private connector. No wrap/unwrap entries in the subscription Activity Log during the window. suspicious it’s an RBAC or diag setting thing. timeline: ~2025-10-18T14:22Z to 14:30Z

alice.support: sorry to hear that. quick clarifying q's: 1) Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM? 2) private endpoint enabled? 3) is the SPN in the same subscription/tenant as the vault or cross-subscription? and can you paste the approximate timestamps?

ben.customer: single-tenant Key Vault (not HSM), private endpoint yes. SPN is a service principal in a different subscription but same tenant. failures 2025-10-18T14:22:00Z — 14:30:00Z. we rotated the key and updated the KID in our app config.

carla.secops: common culprits: (A) the new key version not granted data-plane permissions (wrapKey/unwrapKey), (B) diagnostic settings not configured for KeyVaultAudit so you won't see data-plane ops, (C) private endpoint DNS or network rules blocking calls to monitor/log endpoints.

alice.support: couple quick checks: confirm the SPN has key permissions (get/wrapKey/unwrapKey) and whether the vault uses RBAC or Access Policies mode. also verify the exact kid string your runtime is requesting (should include version suffix).

dave.engineer: run these az CLI commands to inspect: 
```
az role assignment list --assignee <SPN_APP_ID> --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault>
az keyvault key show --name <key-name> --vault-name <vault> --query "key.kid"
az keyvault key list --vault-name <vault> --query "[].attributes" --output table
```
if the vault uses access policies instead of RBAC, check and set: 
```
az keyvault show --name <vault> --query properties.enableRbacAuthorization
az keyvault set-policy --name <vault> --spn <SPN_APP_ID> --key-permissions get wrapKey unwrapKey
```

ben.customer: how do i quickly tell if diagnostics are capturing wrap/unwrap? I only enabled Activity Log retention previously.

erin.docs: for Key Vault you need Diagnostic Settings on the vault resource and enable both management plane and data plane categories (AuditEvent / KeyVaultAudit / KeyVaultLogs depending on vault). example az monitor snippet: 
```
az monitor diagnostic-settings create --name kv-diagnostics --resource /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault> --logs '[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true},{"category":"KeyVaultAudit","enabled":true}]' --workspace <log-workspace-id>
```
note category names vary by vault sku/version; double-check portal.

alice.support: other private-ep gotchas: ensure the Private DNS zone resolves to the private IP from your connector VNet, and check NSGs/route tables that might block outbound traffic to Log Analytics endpoints if you're routing logs. also ensure role assignment scope is the vault resource (not only subscription scope) for cross-subscription SPNs.

ben.customer: ran az role assignment — SPN has "Key Vault Crypto User" on the vault scope in subscription A (vault is in sub A). Redwood Private runs in subscription B. i also ran a manual wrap/unwrap from a jumpbox using the SPN and it succeeded. but app still logs unwrap failures.

dave.engineer: two more diagnostics to check: 1) confirm the KID that the connector sent in the failing requests matches the vault key id (including version). our runtime requires exact match. 2) token/credential caching — if you rotated SPN creds recently the connector might have a cached token or stale claim; restarting the connector/agent clears this.

carla.secops: once you enable diagnostics, query KeyVaultAudit in your workspace for operations around the timestamp: 
```
KeyVaultAudit
| where TimeGenerated between (datetime(2025-10-18T14:15:00Z) .. datetime(2025-10-18T14:40:00Z))
| where OperationName contains "wrap" or OperationName contains "unwrap" or OperationName contains "decrypt"
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, ResultType, Identity, Properties
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
```
if you see nothing, the vault isn't emitting data-plane logs or diagnostic settings aren't wired.

ben.customer: enabled KeyVaultAudit and now I can see unwrap attempts — several with `StatusCode: 403, Error: \"Insufficient key permissions\"` at 2025-10-18T14:22:05Z. that explains it.

alice.support: ok root cause looks like the new key version lacked explicit data-plane permissions for the SPN. remediation: 1) grant the SPN get/wrapKey/unwrapKey on the key or vault (access policy or RBAC mapping that includes key ops), 2) ensure diagnostics stay enabled, 3) when rotating keys, update KID and restart connectors to avoid cached versions/tokens, 4) validate DNS/network for private endpoints and log egress.

erin.docs: recommended runbook checklist for BYOK rotations: 
- confirm diagnostics (KeyVaultAudit) enabled and forwarding to LA workspace
- validate SPN/key permissions (wrap/unwrap/get) at the resource/key level
- update app KID to the exact versioned key id and run manual wrap/unwrap test with SPN before traffic cutover
- schedule connector restart window in case of token cache issues
- document rollback path (repoint to previous key version)
example commands to include in your runbook: 
```
az role assignment create --assignee <SPN_APP_ID> --role "Key Vault Crypto User" --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault>
az keyvault set-policy --name <vault> --spn <SPN_APP_ID> --key-permissions get wrapKey unwrapKey
```

ben.customer: adding these steps now. planning to grant the permissions and restart the connector. thanks! :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: connector restart requested by ben.customer at 2025-10-18T15:05:00Z. status: scheduled.

alice.support: closing thread — please reopen if anything unexpected. we'll update our onboarding/BYOK docs to emphasize KeyVaultAudit and private endpoint caveats.
